export_checks: 115 solver summaries in the sweep folder, 23 per level, no task twice and no orphan attempt folder; the 69 Max attempts the Fable usage limit refused hold no summary and are kept apart; the sweep log shows each level complete and the Max resume after the limit reset

every run is claude-code:claude-fable-5-2 at its requested level on Claude Code 2.1.321 in auto permission mode with safe mode, from bench/2026-11-09-fable52-frontier-v4 with a clean source block and every task hash equal to the frozen suite lock; every reply in every stream was served by claude-fable-5-2
every integrity audit: no web, no benchmark data or answer-key paths, not contaminated

each run's tokens and thinking tokens summed over every result receipt in the archived stream (whose hash matches), and its session list-price total, equal the population record; exactly two runs have two receipts
the population records' hashes and the manifests' hashes equal those frozen in v3.30.2 and v3.30.3, Muse's manifests are byte-identical, and every run's summary hash equals its manifest entry
rubric, prompts, schemas, seed, repeats, gate allowance, weights, retry rule, control hashes and both judges' pins equal the published v3.27 record

Muse Spark 1.3 (v3.30) and GPT-6.1 Sol (v3.30.2) passed every calibration gate with no allowance; Grok 4.6 failed g14_pair_2_1 under v3.30 and judged nothing; no reviewer fallback; no operator marker; twelve Sol answer-key matches recovered under recover_one_based_indexes and one Muse probe excerpt re-wrapped

per-row Code quality, both combined scores and each judge's single-judge score recomputed and matched to the frozen summaries; each level's means and standard errors, per-judge means included, matched to the summaries' groups

combined score, its standard error, Code quality, tasks passed, minutes and cost per level matched to the harness card table; the cards are byte-identical to the harness copies and the card record names both published summaries
no dashes, NUL characters or host paths in exported text
limits: Claude Fable 5.2 is judged by Muse Spark 1.3 and GPT-6.1 Sol. The Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 board rows keep their published Muse Spark 1.3 and Grok 4.6 scores; the comparison card shows them under a matched Muse and Sol panel from comparison-only rounds v3.30.4 and v3.30.5, and GPT-6 Astra with its published Muse and Grok scores, because Sol shares its lab. Scores from different panels are not calibrated against each other.
GPT-6.1 Sol reviews Fable 5.2 about 7 points higher than Muse Spark 1.3 does at every level; the published score is their mean and combined_single_judge gives each judge alone.
Grok 4.6 failed its v3.30 calibration exam (gate g14_pair_2_1), so the usual Muse and Grok panel could not judge.

Runs used --thinking-display summarized so traces keep thinking summaries, a run condition earlier Claude columns did not have; the summaries are withheld because they describe the reference programs.
The Fable usage limit refused the first Max attempts; they did no work and are not part of the population. Max ran from November 10 at 23:14 to November 11 at 13:28 PST after the limit reset.
Two run summaries count only the last of two result receipts and no summary records thinking tokens (adapter issues); every figure here is summed from the raw streams, and grading is unaffected.
Thirteen judge answers went through frozen recovery rules (twelve Sol index shifts, one Muse excerpt re-wrap); none changes a score.
Frontier Code quality is the reviewed layer plus intent recovery and is never compared with Routine v1 Code quality.
One attempt per task and level, on the owner's Mac, local sandbox, flat 3-hour task bound, one task at a time.
publication_scope: Per-run scores, per-panel sub-scores, aggregates, judge protocol text, calibration verdicts and control means, integrity-audit verdicts, raw and thinking tokens, tool-call counts and list-price cost.
withheld: quirk answer keys (they describe hidden-test behaviour)
reviewer session identifiers and usage receipts
solver event streams (a structure-only redacted trace of every run is public in the vulcanbench-fable52-traces repository)
integrity_limit: Hash checks bind the export to frozen files; they do not prove that judges were unbiased or that no training overlap exists.
